nodes.title: Hierapolis geared stone saw
nodes.anchor_rationale: The ancient public monument presents an inscription and relief interpreted as a water-powered twin stone saw; the monument is evidence of historical public representation of the proposed mechanism.
nodes.entry_community: People viewing the roadside funerary monument at Hierapolis

entry_scope.configuration: A waterwheel and gearing depicted with two stone-saw frames on M. Aurelius Ammianos’s sarcophagus; the crank-and-rod mechanism and operation are archaeological reconstruction.

entry_evidence.supports: Third-century roadside relief and inscription depict and attribute the geared wheel, rods and twin saws; crank and operating reconstruction are interpretive.

nodes.entry_uncertainty: The relief and inscription survive, not the depicted machine. Its reconstruction, working operation and stylistic third-century dating remain uncertain; awareness through this representation is not evidence of practical adoption.
nodes.proxy_justification: No physical sawmill or direct operating record establishes community use of this exact configuration; the dated roadside monument supplies only a bounded proxy for public exposure to its representation.

links.statement: Watson and Crick explicitly cited Wyatt’s base-ratio measurements among the chemical observations consistent with complementary pairing.
links.temporal_note: Measurements reported by 1 July 1952 precede the 1953 double-helix proposal; the report does not establish the experiments’ earliest date.

links.statement: Hydration-dependent fibre diffraction supplied the patterns from which Franklin and Gosling inferred B-form geometry.
links.temporal_note: Earlier exposures and subsequent interpretation overlap in the evidence; the inference was documented by 1953, without an established date of first formulation.

links.statement: The consortium cited Prober’s dye-labelled terminators among production-enabling laboratory advances.
links.temporal_note: The demonstration reported by October 1987 precedes the later described production workflow; the demonstration’s earliest date is unresolved.

links.statement: The purified enzyme reaction and assay made it possible to investigate DNA-dependent synthesis outside intact cells.
links.temporal_note: Preparation documented by October 1957 precedes the later evidence synthesis.

links.statement: Mapped-clone sequencing and assembly generated the public human draft analysed from the October 2000 snapshot.
links.temporal_note: Production and resulting draft overlap; the endpoint is a snapshot, not a later all-gaps-closed milestone.

links.statement: Kornberg used complementary pairing in the Watson–Crick model to interpret template-directed enzymatic synthesis.
links.temporal_note: 1953 proposed model precedes the 1958–1959 biochemical account.

links.statement: The original φX174 genome report explicitly used the plus/minus sequence-reading method.
links.temporal_note: The method demonstration was documented by December 1974, before the 1977 genome-sequence report.

links.statement: Sanger, Nicklen and Coulson presented chain termination as a further polymerase sequencing method related to plus/minus.
links.temporal_note: Earlier plus/minus development is distinct from the later 1977 method.

links.statement: The consortium identified four-colour fluorescence detection, citing Smith et al., among the advances supporting automated reads.
links.temporal_note: The demonstrated readout predates production-scale refinements.

links.statement: The plus/minus assay requires complementary template copying because its sequence readout comes from primer-extension products.
links.temporal_note: Established copying operation precedes its later assay use.

links.statement: Prober’s system adapted dideoxy sequencing with four fluorescent terminators and a combined reaction/readout.
links.temporal_note: The 1977 termination publication preceded the 1987 modified-system report; these publication dates are not exact dates of the experiments.

links.statement: The physically isolated 1960 Micrologic sample was a development antecedent of the Type F flip-flop made available in March 1961; this does not identify that particular prototype die or its isolation as the earliest sold configuration.
links.temporal_note: Prototype May 1960 preceded evaluation sales in March 1961.

links.statement: The 1959 Fairchild planar prototype preceded the commercial 2N1613 in development of the planar transistor.
links.temporal_note: Prototype preceded 1960 commercial sale.

links.statement: Ørsted and Esmarck used the stronger twenty-trough battery to repeat and extend initially inconclusive needle-deflection trials.
links.temporal_note: The working battery and the observations belong to the same 1820 programme; apparatus use precedes the resulting observation within the year.

links.statement: Marconi reports using a Branly coherer alongside the Hertz oscillator, then changing the filings detector because the initial version was unreliable.
links.temporal_note: The receiving development follows the source development.

links.statement: The dielectric-polarization problem guided Hertz’s choice and revision of primary/secondary conductor geometry and insulator insertion tests after a chance spark observation provided a usable method.
links.temporal_note: The receiving development follows the source development.

links.statement: The rapid oscillator and spark-gap secondary conductor, reused with a reflecting metal wall, made spatial wave/reflection patterns observable.
links.temporal_note: The receiving development follows the source development.

links.statement: Marconi reports beginning his signalling trials with an ordinary Hertz oscillator, adapting a laboratory wave source to a communications objective.
links.temporal_note: The receiving development follows the source development.

links.statement: Faraday’s investigations of induced currents supplied an explicitly acknowledged empirical foundation for Maxwell’s field equations.
links.temporal_note: The receiving development follows the source development.

links.statement: Marconi’s 1895 trials progressed through detector and reflector arrangements to the reported August configuration with elevated conductors and earth connections at both ends.
links.temporal_note: Both endpoints anchor to 1895; the source explicitly distinguishes early trials from the August arrangement.

links.statement: Obtaining currents from magnets prompted Faraday to adapt Arago’s rotating-metal experiment into an electrical source, culminating in the disc and collectors.
links.temporal_note: The same-year report explicitly places success in magnet-current tests before the stated generator objective, while rearranging detailed trials.

links.statement: The 1879 dielectric test programme sought evidence for assumptions connecting older electromagnetic laws with Maxwell’s equations.
links.temporal_note: The receiving development follows the source development.

links.statement: Last’s project implemented the monolithic approach specified by Noyce’s patent.
links.temporal_note: July 1959 filing precedes project initiation and 1960 implementation.

links.statement: Ørsted’s current–needle demonstration stimulated Ampère’s investigation of attraction and repulsion between current-carrying wires.
links.temporal_note: Both endpoints are in 1820: Ørsted’s July report precedes Ampère’s September/October presentations.

links.statement: Maxwell explicitly identifies Ørsted’s action of currents on a magnet as an empirical foundation of his field equations.
links.temporal_note: The receiving development follows the source development.

links.statement: Faraday recreated Ørsted’s experiment while reviewing electromagnetism, then made new equipment that produced continuous rotation.
links.temporal_note: The receiving development follows the source development.

links.statement: Andrus and Bond applied photoresist patterning to Frosch and Derick’s oxide-mask process.
links.temporal_note: Both nodes are 1955; the source states the dependency, so year-level overlap is not a reversed chronology.

links.statement: Thermally grown oxide’s improved silicon interface enabled Atalla and Kahng to realize the insulated-gate device.
links.temporal_note: 1958 report precedes the 1959–60 device; overlapping publication periods do not imply reverse use.

links.statement: The same flip-flop programme progressed from physical isolation to a working junction-isolated production approach.
links.temporal_note: Exact dates establish May before September despite equal year anchors.

links.statement: Hoerni’s retained-oxide proposal was developed into a working planar transistor.

links.statement: Noyce extended Hoerni’s retained-oxide idea by using the oxide as insulation beneath circuit interconnections.
links.temporal_note: The source is the 1957 conception, avoiding a false claim that the March 1959 demonstration caused an earlier 1959 idea.

links.statement: Last’s IC project explicitly used Hoerni’s planar process to fabricate its circuit components.
links.temporal_note: March transistor precedes the August project and May 1960 circuit.

links.statement: Faraday extended the induction investigation from changing an iron core’s magnetization to moving a permanent magnet, testing whether formation of a magnet was essential.

links.statement: Faggin carried silicon-gate expertise to Intel and added logic-process features used to implement the 4004.
links.temporal_note: 1968 deployment and 1970 transfer precede the 1971 CPU.

links.statement: Bardeen’s explanation directed the surface experiments that led to the Bardeen–Brattain amplifier.
links.temporal_note: Hypothesis in 1946–47 precedes the December 1947 experiment.

links.statement: Atalla and colleagues explicitly used the surface-state/space-charge framework and credited Bardeen when interpreting treated surfaces.
links.temporal_note: 1947 published theory precedes the 1958–59 experiments/report.

links.statement: A branch previously supplying Arelate was redirected to supply the Barbegal mills.
links.temporal_note: Earlier node records city-supply use through c. 120; receiving node records subsequent diversion c. 120–130.

links.statement: Shen describes using two such forms alternately and releasing the types by reheating after use.
links.temporal_note: An operational dependency within one reign-bounded account; no later observation is made to unlock an earlier device.

links.statement: The constructed Hōkūleʻa was the vessel Mau guided on the 1976 passage to Tahiti.
links.temporal_note: Launch precedes the specified deployment.

links.statement: The team used a comparison-based hypothesis about earlier canoe forms to select Hōkūleʻa’s design.
links.temporal_note: 1973 design work precedes the documented 1975 launch.

links.statement: Hōkūleʻa served as the physical experimental platform on which the navigation methods were tested at sea.
links.temporal_note: Documented 1975 launch precedes 1980 experimental use.

links.statement: Korent’s identifications of salient wave patterns guided where the researchers deployed the directional buoy.

links.statement: The participants applied Mau’s taught integration of sea and sky cues in the 1980 navigation trial.
links.temporal_note: The dated instruction precedes the field test.

links.statement: Later basalt walls modified the sides of the previously excavated F10 channel.

links.statement: Latitude cues investigated in the planetarium were taken to sea and tested during the 1980 voyage.
links.temporal_note: The study node is dated by departure; process order within 1980 is explicit.

links.statement: After aqueduct cuts stopped the hill mills, Belisarius installed customary mill machinery between boats driven by the Tiber.

links.statement: Following debris damage, an upstream chain barrier and removal crew were added; continued use of the river mills is reported.

links.statement: The reported form combines separately fired character types with a coated plate and retaining frame.

links.statement: Directional buoy spectra supplied measured wave components for comparison with the navigator-identified sea state.
links.temporal_note: Instrument deployments and resulting observations belong to the same bounded campaign.

links.statement: Powell and Lealand paired their own-formula objective with eyepieces constructed on Abbe’s plan, according to Dallinger’s contemporary account.
links.temporal_note: The Jena introduction preceded the reported English November exhibition within 1886.

links.statement: Thomas and Gilchrist changed the Bessemer converter lining to address phosphorus in the feedstock.
links.temporal_note: The base converter precedes the documented modifications by two decades.

links.statement: Göransson’s Edsken work implemented the named Bessemer method at practical scale.
links.temporal_note: The 1856 patent precedes the 1858 implementation.

links.statement: Dallinger put the compensating eyepieces on both new and existing objectives, allowing him to distinguish an eyepiece contribution from the merits of the initial Zeiss objective.
links.temporal_note: The 1886 eyepieces were available before the comparisons reported in early 1887.

links.statement: Faraday used the Royal Institution installation for the continuing glass experiments that turned specifically to heavy fusible glasses in September 1828.
links.temporal_note: The installation precedes the specialized heavy-glass work by about a year.

links.statement: Durrer advised VÖEST on top blowing following technical contact with Gerlafingen; Linz then ran its own trials.
links.temporal_note: Gerlafingen’s 1948 experiment precedes Linz’s 1949 trials.

links.statement: Faraday explicitly identifies the heavy optical glass from his earlier research as the material with which he first obtained magnetic rotation of polarized light.
links.temporal_note: The glass preparation was reported in 1829; its documented magneto-optical use is in 1845.

links.statement: Zeiss reports using the Jena materials together with new lens formulae to manufacture the objective series introduced in 1886.
links.temporal_note: Both nodes have 1886 availability dates; the texts establish supply and design use before the instrument introduction within that year.

links.statement: Successful converter tests prompted construction of production plants, including Linz’s 1952 LD works.
links.temporal_note: Three years separate the trial stage from plant operation.

links.statement: Zeiss introduced special compensating eyepieces for use with its new objective series; Abbe explains their coordinated correction of color-dependent magnification.
links.temporal_note: Both components were introduced together in 1886; this edge records combination, not chronological succession.

links.statement: CB3 combines the treated iron shaft with a bronze head.
links.temporal_note: Dates coincide: component preparation precedes assembly within one object, not a claimed centuries-long development.

links.statement: Abbe says that the measured composition–optical-property relations guided glass syntheses and that the Jena supply operation resulted from these experiments.

links.statement: A Zeiss 1/8-inch objective lent through Frank Crisp, followed by a maker-supplied series, furnished the instruments Dallinger compared with his existing optics.

links.statement: News of a Dutch spyglass, confirmed from Paris, prompted Galileo to make and improve a similar instrument.
links.temporal_note: The public Dutch episode in 1608 precedes Galileo's 1609 construction; later improvements continue into 1610.

links.statement: Oughtred put two Gunter-type scales alongside one another and moved them relatively, dispensing with separate dividers.

links.statement: Briggs read Napier's published work, discussed changes with him, and calculated the revised logarithms published in 1617.
links.temporal_note: The 1614 source publication precedes discussions and the 1617 receiving publication.

links.statement: Logarithmic calculation was embodied in Gunter's physical scales, where distances support multiplication and division.
links.temporal_note: The mathematical publication predates the museum's 1620 introduction date.

links.statement: Oughtred’s sliding-scale approach developed into a circular form; Allen influenced its redesign into fixed scales with paired radial arms and made the Whipple 0833 example at the target event.
links.temporal_note: The 1620s concept and 1632 description precede the approximately dated surviving object.

links.statement: Newton says his diagnosis of unequal refraction led him to consider reflection and then build a metal-mirror telescope.
links.temporal_note: The earlier experiments are dated by the 1672 account; the 1668 device precedes publication of that account.

links.statement: An improved instrument let Galileo see objects near Jupiter that weaker instruments had not revealed; repeated observations supported the satellite interpretation.
links.temporal_note: The suitable improved instrument was already in use on 7 January within the development interval; publication followed in March.

links.statement: Galileo's improved telescope resolved lunar light-shadow details used to infer elevations and depressions.
links.temporal_note: The late-1609 instrument state predates these observations; the source instrument interval also covers further improvements for 1610 work.

links.statement: While studying with Ibn al-Banna, al-Hawari reproduced his rules and supplied numerical examples, including explicit place-by-place addition.
links.temporal_note: The source rulebook was complete before 1301; teaching and example-writing occurred by the recorded 1305 completion.

links.statement: Al-Uqlidisi describes adapting board-style calculation to ink and paper without erasing, including a mixed-sign multiplication layout.

links.statement: Leonardo links his instruction at Bugia and later study of Indian calculation methods to his decision to compose Liber abaci; its revised text explicitly teaches positional numerals and zero.
links.temporal_note: Instruction precedes initial composition; content is shown at the surviving revision's date to avoid backdating details.

links.statement: Liber Alchorismi is a distinct Latin reworking of the al-Khwarizmi-derived arithmetic tradition, with expanded exposition and reordered operations.
links.temporal_note: Both surviving Latin traditions have broad twelfth-century dates; the edge comes from the earlier Arabic-source node and does not impose an unsupported order on the Latin branches.

links.statement: The lost Arabic arithmetic was translated into Latin and reworked into the tradition witnessed by Dixit Algorizmi.
links.temporal_note: The original work precedes the twelfth-century translation; thirteenth-century witnesses do not redate the translation.

links.statement: Wilkinson's large-cylinder machining supplied Bloomfield's 50-inch cylinder; the technical history associates this scale of supply with his stationary-cylinder through-bar arrangement.
links.temporal_note: Production occurs in the 1775–76 supply interval and before engine operation; overlapping intervals reflect uncertain machine dating, not a later cause.

links.statement: The falling-weight calorimetric apparatus, calibrated thermometers and correction measurements supplied the work and heating quantities in Joule’s refined estimate.
links.temporal_note: Physical measurements precede the reported synthesis; both anchors are the same dated report, not asserted manufacture dates.

links.statement: Clapeyron named Carnot's 1824 work as his starting point and recast its heat-engine argument using mathematical analysis and pressure–volume geometry.
links.temporal_note: 1824 publication precedes the 1834 memoir; 1837 is the consulted translation date, not the event date.

links.statement: Clausius stated that he knew Carnot’s work through Clapeyron and Thomson, and identified Clapeyron’s analytical treatment as a source for the 1850 investigation.
links.temporal_note: 1834/1837 text precedes 1850 use; the later 1864 statement of direct access is excluded.

links.statement: Thomson compared Clapeyron’s tabulated heat-engine values with Regnault-derived values in the appendix read 30 April 1849.
links.temporal_note: Clapeyron’s earlier table precedes the separately dated April appendix; this comparison is not assigned to the January presentation.

links.statement: Thomson stated that he knew Carnot’s theory through Clapeyron’s paper and used that theory in his 1848 thermometric-scale proposal.
links.temporal_note: 1834 original and 1837 translation precede the 1848 proposal.

links.statement: Thomson acknowledged Clausius’s proof of the reversible-engine proposition, attributed one foundational proposition jointly to Carnot and Clausius, and compared their heat-flow axioms.
links.temporal_note: Clausius’s 1850 work precedes acknowledged use in 1851; Thomson’s claimed independent conception is kept separate.
